arxiv-2001-02137.creator: Ruggero Freddi
arxiv-2001-02137.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Ruggero Freddi. In this paper we consider the Dirichlet problem (0.1) { − Δ ​ u = ρ 2 ​ ( e u − e − u ) in ​ Ω u = 0 on ​ ∂ Ω , \begin{cases}-\Delta u=\rho^{2}(e^{u}-e^{-u})&\text{ in }\Omega\\ u=0&\text{ on }\partial\Omega,\end{cases} where ρ \rho is a small parameter and Ω \Omega is a C 2 C^{2} bounded domain in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} .

arxiv-2108-00834.title: Application of pattern spectra and convolutional neural networks to the analysis of simulated Cherenkov Telescope Array data
arxiv-2108-00834.creator: M. H. F. Wilkinson
arxiv-2108-00834.description: Abstract The Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA) will be the next generation gamma-ray observatory and will be the major global instrument for very-high-energy astronomy over the next decade, offering 5 − 10 5-10 × \times better flux sensitivity than current generation gamma-ray telescopes.

arxiv-2306-09983.title: Evaluating Superhuman Models with Consistency Checks
arxiv-2306-09983.creator: Lukas Fluri, Daniel Paleka, Florian Tramèr
arxiv-2306-09983.description: Abstract If machine learning models were to achieve superhuman abilities at various reasoning or decision-making tasks, how would we go about evaluating such models, given that humans would necessarily be poor proxies for ground truth? In this paper, we propose a framework for evaluating superhuman models via consistency checks .

arxiv-2310-06459.title: New physics search via CP observables in B s 0 → ϕ ​ ϕ B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow\phi\phi decay with Chromomagnetic operators
arxiv-2310-06459.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the time-dependent angular analysis of B s 0 → ϕ ​ ϕ B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow\phi\phi decay to search for new physics signals via CP-violating observables. We work with a new physics Hamiltonian containing both left- and right-handed Chromomagnetic dipole operators.

arxiv-2311-00203.title: Modeling subjectivity (by Mimicking Annotator Annotation) in toxic comment identification across diverse communities WARNING: This paper contains comments that are offensive by nature.
arxiv-2311-00203.creator: Senjuti Dutta, Sid Mittal, Sherol Chen, Deepak Ramachandran, Ravi Rajakumar, Ian Kivlichan, Sunny Mak, Alena Butryna, Praveen Paritosh
arxiv-2311-00203.description: Abstract The prevalence and impact of toxic discussions online have made content moderation crucial. Automated systems can play a vital role in identifying toxicity, and reducing the reliance on human moderation. Nevertheless, identifying toxic comments for diverse communities continues to present challenges that are addressed in this paper.

arxiv-2402-02299.title: A Review and Comparison of AI Enhanced Side Channel Analysis Journal: JETC Volume: 1 1 1 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3517810 Thanks: Corresponding Author: Yier Jin CCS: Hardware Integrated circuits CCS: Security and privacy Cryptanalysis and other attacks CCS: Computing methodologies Artificial inte
arxiv-2402-02299.creator: Max Panoff, Honggang Yu, Haoqi Shan, Yier Jin
arxiv-2402-02299.description: Abstract . Side Channel Analysis (SCA) presents a clear threat to privacy and security in modern computing systems. The vast majority of communications are secured through cryptographic algorithms. These algorithms are often provably-secure from a cryptographical perspective, but their implementation on real hardware introduces vulnerabilities.

arxiv-2409-02029.title: Bulk-boundary correspondence from Hyperinvariant tensor networks
arxiv-2409-02029.creator: Rafał Bistroń 1,2, Mykhailo Hontarenko 1 and, Karol Życzkowski 1,3
arxiv-2409-02029.description: Abstract We introduce a tensor network designed to faithfully simulate the AdS/CFT correspondence, akin to the multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA), following hyper-invariant tensor network. The proposed construction integrates bulk indices within the network architecture to uphold the key features of the HaPPY code, including complementary recovery.

arxiv-2506-15566.title: Task-Agnostic Experts Composition for Continual Learning
arxiv-2506-15566.creator: Luigi Quarantiello, Andrea Cossu, Vincenzo Lomonaco
arxiv-2506-15566.description: Abstract Compositionality is one of the fundamental abilities of the human reasoning process, that allows to decompose a complex problem into simpler elements. Such property is crucial also for neural networks, especially when aiming for a more efficient and sustainable AI framework.

arxiv-2510-21340.title: Koopman Mode Decomposition of Thermodynamic Dissipation in Nonlinear Langevin Dynamics
arxiv-2510-21340.creator: Daiki Sekizawa, Sosuke Ito, Masafumi Oizumi
arxiv-2510-21340.description: Abstract Nonlinear oscillations are commonly observed in complex systems far from equilibrium, such as living organisms. These oscillations are essential for sustaining vital processes, like neuronal firing, circadian rhythms, and heartbeats. In such systems, thermodynamic dissipation is necessary to maintain oscillations against noise.

arxiv-2602-05692.title: MedErrBench: A Fine-Grained Multilingual Benchmark for Medical Error Detection and Correction with Clinical Expert Annotations
arxiv-2602-05692.creator: Congbo Ma, Yichun Zhang, Yousef Al-Jazzazi, Ahamed Foisal, Laasya Sharma, Yousra Sadqi, Khaled Saleh, Jihad Mallat, Farah E. Shamout
arxiv-2602-05692.description: Abstract Inaccuracies in existing or generated clinical text may lead to serious adverse consequences, especially if it is a misdiagnosis or incorrect treatment suggestion. With Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly being used across diverse healthcare applications, comprehensive evaluation through dedicated benchmarks is crucial. However, such datasets remain scarce, especially across diverse languages and contexts.

arxiv-2602-12847.title: DPUConfig: Optimizing ML Inference in FPGAs Using Reinforcement Learning The research is co-funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe Programme under the MLSysOps Project (Grant Agreement No. 101092912). It is also conducted in the operating framework of the University of Thessaly Innovation, Te
arxiv-2602-12847.creator: Alexandros Patras, Spyros Lalis, Christos D. Antonopoulos, and Nikolaos Bellas
arxiv-2602-12847.description: Abstract Heterogeneous embedded systems, with diverse computing elements and accelerators such as FPGAs, offer a promising platform for fast and flexible ML inference, which is crucial for services such as autonomous driving and augmented reality, where delays can be costly. However, efficiently allocating computational resources for deep learning applications in FPGA-based systems is a challenging task.

pmc-10610289.title: Novel Baicalein-Derived Inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum
pmc-10610289.creator: Chandra Sekhar Gudla, Vignesh Selvam, Siva Shanmugam Selvaraj, Renu Tripathi, Prince Joshi, Salique Hassan Shaham, Mayas Singh, Radha Krishan Shandil, Saman Habib, Shridhar Narayanan, Nicolò Musso, Andrea Marino
pmc-10610289.description: Malaria, a life-threatening mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, continues to pose a significant global health burden. Despite notable progress in combating the disease in recent years, malaria remains prevalent in many regions, particularly in Southeast Asia and most of sub-Saharan Africa, where it claims hundreds of thousands of lives annually.

pmc-10656492.title: Uric acid as a mediator in the correlation between white blood cells and preeclampsia severity: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-10656492.creator: Bai-jia Li, Ting-ting Zhu, Xiao-ying Hu, Chao-man He
pmc-10656492.description: This study aimed to analyze the independent risk factors for predicting preeclampsia severity and explore its underlying mechanism. Clinical data of patients with preeclampsia were collected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV database. Univariate and multivariate analyses were employed to assess the significant factors associated with preeclampsia severity.

pmc-10753232.title: Fractal analysis in cardiovascular magnetic resonance: prognostic value of biventricular trabecular complexity in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
pmc-10753232.creator: Wen-Yi Jiang, Bing-Hua Chen, Chen Zhang, Ruo-Yang Shi, Rui Wu, Dong-Aolei An, Xiao-Hai Ma, Luke Wesemann, Jiani Hu, Yan Zhou, Jian-Rong Xu, Lei Zhao, Lian-Ming Wu
pmc-10753232.description: BackgroundTrabecular complexity can be quantified by fractal analysis based on cine images of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), yielding fractal dimension (FD) index. We aimed to investigate the prognostic value of biventricular FD in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM).MethodsThis retrospective study included 284 (192 men, median age 53 years) patients with HCM who underwent CMR, with median follow-up of 24 months.

pmc-11075023.title: Lipid Metabolic Disorders in Neurodegenerative Diseases – Role of Androgen Receptor
pmc-11075023.creator: Satvika Sharma, Avneet Saini, D.K. Dhawan
pmc-11075023.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The challenge of managing neurodegenerative disorders is a worldwide concern, especially in the aging population. Neurodegenerative diseases are a varied group of disorders that are characterized by progressive degeneration of the structure and function of the nerve cells. Neurodegenerative diseases are increasing at an alarming rate, and hence there is an urgent need for an in-depth analysis of various metabolic malfunctions that alter the proper functioning of a cell.

pmc-11329896.title: ‘There is no such word as palliative care for us at the moment’: A mixed-method study exploring the perceptions of healthcare professionals on the need for palliative care in Bhutan
pmc-11329896.creator: Tara Devi Laabar, Christobel Saunders, Kirsten Auret, Claire E. Johnson
pmc-11329896.description: Background:The need for palliative care is ever-increasing globally. However, it is least developed or not available in most low-and-middle-income-countries including Bhutan.Objective:This study was aimed at exploring the perspectives of Bhutanese healthcare professionals on the need for palliative care in the country.Design:This is a cross-sectional, mixed-method study.

pmc-11331989.title: Both partners’ negative emotion drives aggression during couples’ conflict
pmc-11331989.creator: Annah G McCurry, Robert C May, David I Donaldson
pmc-11331989.description: Researchers examining conflict between intimate partners believe that the experience and expression of emotion drives aggressive behaviour. Intra-personally, increases in negative affect make aggression more likely. Inter-personally, theoretical models suggest that each individuals’ perception of their partners’ emotion also influences aggression, potentially creating a Violence Escalation Cycle.

pmc-11587432.title: Unveiling the Burden: A Six-Year Retrospective Analysis of Pressure Ulcer Epidemiology in a ICU
pmc-11587432.creator: Sofia Vieira, António Mostardinha, Paulo Alves, Richard Gray
pmc-11587432.description: Objective: This study describes the epidemiological changes in pressure ulcers (PUs) in a Portuguese intensive care unit (ICU) from January 2017 to June 2023, characterizes critically ill patients with PUs, identifies specific risk factors, and assesses the effectiveness of implemented preventive measures.

pmc-13343858.title: Vincular Project: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial with changes in 24-h movement behaviors targeting the reduce of depressive symptoms in adults
pmc-13343858.creator: Cecília Bertuol, Deborah Kazimoto Alves, Giovani Firpo Del Duca
pmc-13343858.description: BackgroundA better understanding of how behavior change interventions work to reduce depressive symptoms, as well as their effects and potential mediators, is needed. This paper described the methods of the Vincular Project, an intervention based on Self-Determination Theory with changes in 24-h movement behaviors (physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep) to reduce depressive symptoms in Brazilian adults.

uslaw-usc-t18-s2235.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2235 — Search warrant procured maliciously
uslaw-usc-t18-s2235.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s2235.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 109 (Searches And Seizures). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever maliciously and without probable cause procures a search warrant to be issued and executed, shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than one year, or both.
